pack.name: EU AI Act core qualification and obligation readiness
pack.source_version: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 consolidated on 27 July 2026 after Regulation (EU) 2026/1744

application_timeline.event: Chapters I and II apply, except the 2026 additions to Article 5
GPAI obligations and the stated governance provisions apply
General application date, subject to Article 113 exceptions
Chapter III Sections 1 to 3 apply to Annex III high-risk systems
Chapter III Sections 1 to 3 apply to Annex I high-risk systems

coverage: all Article 5 prohibited-practice categories, including 2026 additions and application date
all twenty-five Annex III use cases and the Article 6(3) test
high-risk provider, authorised representative, importer, distributor, deployer and value-chain readiness checks
Article 4 AI literacy and Article 50 transparency routes
GPAI model and systemic-risk provider obligations
versioned legal anchors against the consolidated text current on review date

Derived high-risk classification chain: observable screening facts feed rule emissions (Annex III route, Article 6(3) outcome, high-risk status) that downstream obligation rules consume, so no pre-filled legal conclusion is required.
known_gaps: Annex I sectoral product legislation must be assessed in a dedicated sector profile.
The pack does not encode notified-body procedure, market-surveillance powers, regulatory sandboxes, penalties or remedies as operational checklists.
Harmonised standards, common specifications, codes of practice and Commission guidance require separately reviewed releases.
A matched rule is a triage or readiness finding, not a legal opinion or certification.
pack.notice: Application dates are preserved in metadata and findings. Future duties are readiness signals until their stated application date.

fact_catalog.question: Does the composition meet the AI Act definition of an AI system?
Which AI Act operator roles apply to this object or organisation?
Which exact Annex III use-case identifiers apply to the intended purpose?
Which Article 5 routes require detailed element-by-element evaluation?
Which Article 50 transparency routes require detailed evaluation?
Does the system perform profiling of natural persons for Article 6(3)?
Does the Annex III use pose a significant risk of harm to health, safety or fundamental rights?
Does the Annex III use materially influence a decision outcome?
Is the use limited to a narrow procedural task?
Does it improve the result of a previously completed human activity?
Does it detect decision patterns without replacing or influencing the completed human assessment and with proper human review?
Is it limited to a preparatory task for an Annex III assessment?
Does the provider claim the Article 6(3) exception?

Organisation-attested high-risk confirmation. Set directly by a governance decision when one exists; the classification rules emit aiact.high_risk_established from screening facts, so an extractor never proposes this conclusion.
Which route makes the system high-risk (annex_i, annex_iii or both)? Declared by the organisation or emitted by the classification rules; never proposed by an extractor.
Is the AI system a safety component, or itself a covered product, under Annex I legislation?
Does the relevant product legislation require third-party conformity assessment?
Is that third-party assessment required solely for a non-health-and-safety risk excluded by Article 6(1c)?
Does the system deploy subliminal, purposefully manipulative or deceptive techniques?
Do those techniques appreciably impair a person's ability to make an informed decision?
Does the practice materially distort behaviour?
Does the practice cause or reasonably risk significant harm?
Does the system exploit a vulnerability linked to age, disability, or a specific social or economic situation?
Does the system generate or manipulate realistic intimate or sexually explicit material of an identifiable person?
Does the system generate or manipulate child sexual abuse material or a covered performance?
Does the system generate the relevant content?
Does the system manipulate the relevant content?
Does an intimate-content manipulation increase exposure or alter the nature of the depicted activity?
Was freely given, specific, informed, unambiguous and explicit consent obtained?
For a provider, is the content an intended purpose or a reasonably foreseeable reproducible outcome without adequate safeguards?
For a deployer, is the system used for the purpose of generating or manipulating the covered content?
Does a national-law without-right defence apply to the covered material?
Does the system evaluate or classify people over time from social behaviour or personal characteristics?
Does the score lead to detrimental treatment in an unrelated context?
Does the score lead to unjustified or disproportionate detrimental treatment?
Does the system assess or predict a person's risk of committing a criminal offence?

Purpose-taxonomy tags of the composition's active uses. Applied from a validated extraction's proposed uses; never proposed directly as a fact.
Derived: does the Article 6(3) derogation apply? Emitted by the Article 6(3) rule from the screening facts (true on match, false when the conditions demonstrably fail).

Derived: is the high-risk classification established? Emitted by the classification rules, either from the organisation's attested confirmation or from an Annex III route with no Article 6(3) derogation.

anchors.summary: Scope and operator, AI-system, intended-purpose, GPAI-model and other definitions.
Providers and deployers must take context-appropriate measures to support AI literacy.
Complete list of prohibited-practice categories and their stated exceptions and safeguards.
Annex I and Annex III high-risk classification routes and the documented Article 6(3) exception.
Twenty-five high-risk use cases across biometrics, infrastructure, education, employment, services, law enforcement, migration and justice.
Requirements for high-risk systems: risk, data, documentation, logging, transparency, human oversight, accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity.
Provider and value-chain obligations for high-risk AI systems.
Deployer obligations and the fundamental-rights impact assessment.
Registration duties for high-risk and Article 6(3) systems.
Transparency for direct interaction, synthetic content, emotion and biometric systems, deep fakes and public-interest text.
Systemic-risk classification and obligations for GPAI-model providers.
Transitional and staged application dates after the 2026 amendment.

finding.title: Harmful manipulative practice
finding.summary: All cumulative Article 5(1)(a) elements are established by the supplied facts.

obligations.title: Stop the practice and obtain specialist legal review.

finding.summary: The facts match Article 5(1)(ba), subject to the 2 December 2026 application date and the detailed Article 5(1a) and 5(1b) conditions.

rules.title: High-risk status attested by the organisation

finding.title: High-risk classification attested
finding.summary: The organisation attests that the system is high-risk. The attestation is carried forward so every high-risk obligation applies without re-deriving the classification.

reason.matched: aiact.high_risk_confirmed is attested true, so the high-risk status is carried into aiact.high_risk_established.
reason.indeterminate: No attestation is recorded; the derived classification rules decide from the screening facts instead.
reason.not_matched: The organisation has not attested a high-risk status; the derived classification rules decide from the screening facts.

finding.title: Annex III high-risk classification
finding.summary: The use is listed in Annex III (by mapped use case or by purpose tag for the employment points) and the Article 6(3) screening rule concluded the derogation does not apply, so the system is high-risk under Article 6(2). Downstream provider and deployer obligations consume this derived conclusion.
